High on a hilltop in Tuscany’s unspoiled Maremma region, the meticulously restored 14th century
Castello di Segalari offers an authentic taste of Italy.
An aristocratic castle steeped in history, today Castello di Segalari’s ancient ramparts and
stone walls conceal chic contemporary interiors, effortlessly combining original period features
with modern luxury. A perfect setting for families and friends in search of a memorable holiday
rental.
A different side of Tuscany
South of Florence and Siena, Maremma has managed to remain under the tourist radar. Its
beautiful, untamed countryside is dotted with ancient hilltop villages framed by cypress and
olive trees.
Even in the warmth of summer, the area is lush and green. Towards the coast, sweeping plains
have been farmed since Etruscan times, the castle's semi-private beach is mostly untouched,
remaining relatively uncrowded even in high season. Castello di Segalari’s semi-private beach
and newly refurbished beach hut can be enjoyed just ten minutes’ drive from the castle.
Perfectly located
Castello di Segalari is well positioned for those in search of seclusion, while remaining within
easy reach of the region’s many attractions. Pisa (the closest international airport) lies just
40 minutes away, while Florence and Siena are around an hour and a half by car.
Closer to the castle, traditional Tuscan towns and villages are spread across the landscape of
ancient olive groves and rolling vineyards. Within an hour’s drive of the castle lie treasures
such as Massa Marittima and its spectacular cathedral square; ancient Volterra is known for its
artisanal heritage and alabaster carvings, while San Gigmignano is home to 14 medieval towers.
Food and wine
The cuisine here celebrates seasonal ingredients and the region’s diverse landscapes. From the
forests come rich game dishes, while the coast is a bounty for seafood. Chance upon a village
restaurant and you’ll experience the taste of Maremma, such as the family-run La Pineta, with
its warm welcome and dishes including spaghetti alle vongole veraci.
The castle is located in the middle of the sought-after ‘Super Tuscans’ offering velvety,
full-bodied red wines. Only ten minutes from Castello di Segalari, the epicentre of the region's
wine making, Bolgheri is home to iconic, collector favourites such as Sassicaia, Ornellaia and
Masseto.
Your home away from home
Castello di Segalari is a privately-owned home belonging to an internationally-renowned hotel
family. The result is five-star level service, attention to detail and staff on hand, making a
stay here a very special experience.

Each of the castle’s ten spacious guest rooms has its own unique character. Combining a
fresh, modern feel with heritage pieces and artisanal touches, each room is a clever blend
of old and new. Some have canopy beds draped in hand-embroidered fabrics, others boast
lavish marble bathrooms with frescoes on the walls.
Each guest room comes complete with showers and baths, TV, air-conditioning and working
fireplace.
Two of the guest rooms have twin beds and one features three beds – perfect for teenagers or

We have compiled some of our most frequently asked questions. Please contact us with any further queries you may have.
What can I expect from my stay at Castello di Segalari? Castello di Segalari is a luxury historic castle which is only available for bookings in its entirety for exclusive use by the week, or for weddings and special events. There are ten guest rooms in the castle.
Is a minimum stay required?  Yes. The minimum stay is six nights.
Do you have cots or baby beds?  Yes. We have two rooms suitable for children, and we can arrange beds based on the ages of our smallest guests when informed in advance.
Is there Wi-Fi?  Yes. Wi-Fi is available in all of the castle's bedrooms and common areas.
Does the castle have air-conditioning?  Yes. Each bedroom has air-conditioning.
How big is Castello di Segalari?  The interiors of the castle measure a total of 1,500 square meters; there is a 200 sq m terrace and the garden is 7,000 sq m.
What's the capacity of the communal areas? The living room can accommodate 18-20 people. Our table in the dining room comfortably seats up to 14 guests, while the outdoor terrace dining table easily seats 16 guests.
Does the castle have a swimming pool?  Yes. There is an outdoor semi-Olympic swimming pool with massage jets measuring 22 x 7 metres. The pool can be heated (for an extra cost) during the cooler months.
Services & Amenities
Are meals included?  There is a dedicated chef included in the price, however food and beverages requested by guests are billed separately.
Are utility costs included in the price of rental?  Water, gas, electricity and Wi-Fi are included in the price, as is the final cleaning. Any international telephone calls made using the castle's phone are not included and should be paid for separately.
Is the castle fully staffed? The castle comes with a dedicated team (some of whom live on site) including a chef, cleaners and butlers. Housekeeping staff clean the castle between 8am and 4pm and change bed sheets and towels every morning.

Our story
Originally the home of the noble Della Gherardesca family, Castello di Segalari had not been lived in since the 17th century when it was purchased as a family home in the 1980s by its current owners.
Following a meticulous renovation, the medieval castle was restored to its former glory, followed by a more recent revamp under the helm of renowned Spanish architect Julio Lafuente. Today, the castle exudes a contemporary elegance, with sleek interiors and vibrant artworks complementing its grand stonework and vast timber beams.
Inside the castle
The size of the property makes it ideal for groups, family gatherings, milestone birthdays, celebrations and weddings, with ten guest rooms and large spaces for gatherings both inside and out.
The castle’s grand entrance leads to a formal drawing room adorned with antiques and family heirlooms, while the library contains a collection of books waiting to be enjoyed. Despite all its splendour, the castle is a family home that is warm and welcoming. There is a children’s playroom for younger guests and various dining settings for friends and family to choose from. With two dining rooms indoors, one is an intimate space with a striking marble table, while the second is on a grander scale. Outdoors, dining on the terrace or by the pool can be arranged. Guests can look forward to seasonal dishes and Tuscan specialities featuring fresh fish from the Tyrrhenian Sea, locally-reared meat and organically-grown fruit and vegetables from nearby farms and the castle's own vegetable garden.
Explore the grounds
The outdoor terraces deliver panoramic views to the sea and seven islands of the Tuscan archipelago (including Elba, famous for its exiled resident, Napoleon).
With 17 acres of grounds, highlights include a 22-metre long Vermentino marble swimming pool (which can be heated during the cooler months), a tennis court, football pitch, private chapel, numerous outdoor dining areas and a vegetable garden from which the castle’s chef can select fresh ingredients for his dishes.
Just 10 minutes’ drive to the coast and a short walk through the forest lies the castle’s newly refurbished beach hut, Found on a semi-private beach, it offers the perfect spot for a lunchtime picnic or a barbeque under the stars.
Our Team
Along with a team of butlers, cleaners and gardeners, the castle comes with a resident chef who can prepare breakfast, lunch and dinner, or a BBQ under the stars.
Guests can expect a typically warm Italian welcome at Castello di Segalari. It’s what makes a stay here feel both luxurious yet wonderfully relaxed.
Do as much or as little as you desire – from drinking in the views from a poolside lounger to spending the afternoon touring wineries at nearby Bolgheri. While summers here are blissful, the castle is a delight throughout the seasons, with winters made cosy with logs crackling in fireplaces and crisp winter sunshine.
